name: Exact Coefficient-Space Gluing
statement: Let nonempty pieces $C_j\subseteq\{0,1\}^{S\sqcup I_j}$ be downward closed in their pairwise disjoint private blocks and have the same zero section $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^S$. If $X$ is their common-section union and $q=\sum_{j<\ell}|V_j||V_\ell|$ counts pairs of active private coordinates in distinct blocks, then $\mathcal A(X)\cong\{(a^j):a^j\in\mathcal A(C_j),\ r_1(a^1)=\cdots=r_k(a^k)\}\times(\Delta_1^\circ)^q$. The homeomorphism commutes with restriction, so every fixed-section fiber is the product of the piece fibers and the same open-simplex factors. Empty spaces and fibers are included; rational inputs yield an explicit rational positive-margin certificate.
proof: Private downward closure partitions the minimal missing patterns into the common section rows, the nonsection rows belonging to one piece, and positive pairs crossing two active private blocks. Necessity follows by restriction. For sufficiency, scale all supplied piece witnesses by a common $\varepsilon$ and put $-1$ on coordinates outside the occupied block. Choosing $\varepsilon$ below half the smallest private row mass and cross-row coefficient clears every unoccupied-piece and cross-block row while preserving all piece and section inequalities. The row partition is a coordinate identification of the ambient simplex products and therefore gives the stated homeomorphism and its fixed-fiber version.
comments: This is the privately downward finite-arity form of common-section gluing. It records literal agreement of section rows; homotopy types of the pieces alone do not determine the pullback.
